column1: # Who made this pack. Shipped in the manifest so a pack can be credited and traced.
# Columns: name
# A pack is an add-on: it ships, versions and is licensed separately from the app,
# and once packs can come from more than one place a learner has to be able to see
# who made the one they installed. `id` says which pack, `version` says which cut
# of it, and this says who stands behind it.
# A **list**, not a single `author` string, and for the same reason `voices.tsv`
# is a list: content has contributors rather than an owner, they hold different
# roles, and a generated pack's "author" is honestly a tool rather than a person.
# Squashing that into one field is how attribution becomes a lie by omission.
# `role` is free text and describes what this name did — `content`, `engineering`,
# `review`, `generation`. It is not an enum because the honest answer for the next
# pack may be a word this one has no use for.
# `url` is optional and is where a reader can check the claim: a profile, a
# repository, a model card. Leave it off rather than inventing one.
# One rule, and it is the same one `voices.tsv` and the `review` field follow:
# **do not credit a human for generated material.** This pack is machine-generated
# and unreviewed, so the generation is credited as generation and the editorial
# line stays empty until somebody actually reads the Spanish.
Linguastein
Claude (Anthropic)
